recipes.name: Chef John's Ham and Potato Soup
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
1 tablespoon chopped fresh chives for garnish

steps.text: Melt butter in a stockpot over medium heat until golden brown. Stir in carrot, celery, onion, ham, and garlic; cook and stir for 5-6 minutes, until the vegetables soften and the onions are translucent.

Stir in flour; cook for about 3 minutes. Stir in chicken broth, 1 cup at a time. Add water and stir to combine. Turn the heat to high and bring to a simmer. Simmer on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Taste the soup for salt and add more if necessary. Stir in potatoes; cook for 15 minutes, until potatoes are tender. Skim fat if desired.

With a potato masher, mash the soup a few times, leaving plenty of whole chunks of potato. Season with salt and pepper to taste, add cayenne if desired, and add cream. Stir to combine and heat through. Garnish with fresh chives.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Ham and Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: You can never have too many soup recipes. This hearty soup is definitely filling enough to serve as a main course.

review.reviewBody: yum yum yum! made almost exactly to the recipe and was very good. The only change I made was to saute the vegies in water instead of butter in order to reduce the fat and calories. I also used evaporated fat free milk instead of heavy cream. def a keeper, thanks for sharking

We thought it was delicious! The only change I made was using ramps (garlicky green onions) instead of cloves of garlic. Next time I will dice the potatoes larger as it was hard to get much of a mash with that size. (I watched the video and based my dice size by it.) Some family members added sharp shredded cheddar which they said was delicious as well. I served it with baguette bread and oyster crackers. I will make again!!

I always use this with leftover easter ham or even whenever I bake that big smoked ham, I save small bags in the freezer of that cooked ham cubes. I sometimes add gravy and water, or condensed mushroom soup and water (in which case I add cut up cremini or shiitake mushrooms) , instead of soup and water.

This was killer. Tweaked a few things . . . I was using leftover ham that I smoked from Thanksgiving. Used the skin and fat at the beginning and rendered it down. It had a maple bourbon glaze that Caramelized nicely and gave the recipe a hint of spices. Making again today, going to add bacon at the beginning and see how that works.

This is so good! I used an 8oz smoked pork chop and a 1/2 can of evaporated milk since I didn’t have heavy cream. It worked out just fine. I also used red skin potatoes and left the skin on. I microwaved them for 5 minutes before chopping them up and this speeds up the cooking time. Yummy!

This was delicious and could rival any restaurant soup! I had to sub crumbled bacon for ham, and didn’t peel or mash any potatoes. Also used a cup less water, but otherwise followed the ingredient list exactly.

I love just about anything Chef John posts, and this soup didn't disappoint. Excellent. My only changes were to add the ham bone from Christmas dinner, plus some cut-up ham, and I used evaporated milk instead of cream to save on calories. Having it for lunch on a cold, snowy day in Colorado.
I cut out the butter and cream and added a little milk and plain greek yoghurt to comply with my husband's low-fat requirement, and it was still tasty and filling for a cold winter night.
Super allergen friendly. Used smart balance non-dairy butter to saute veggies. Ended up not using creamer (oatmilk) because it was thick and creamy enough. Kids LOVED.

I made this wonderful delicious soup again this year, but I decided to switch it up. I made 6 cups of pork stock from the hambone, the used the other left over ham to finish the recipe as usual. I was worried the hambone stock would be too salty. Nope. In fact, not at all. Man I love cooking with the help of Chef John! Cheers!

Absolutely wonderful!!! I double the recipe and start the cook in my dutch oven. Once it starts getting too full I move some of broth to large crock pot and finish the rest in the dutch oven before combining into crock. Be sure to leave some larger potato chunks. Thank you Chef John!
Easy to make and delicious I have usedour home made venison sausage and WOW amazing simple recipe.
Great soup on a chilly day. The broth is smooth, creamy and delicious. Fairly easy to make!
loved this. I used a ham steak and followed the recipe as written.
Delicious!!!

The seasonings were inadequate. I followed the recipe but it was too liquid and unsavory. I have used some other Chef John recipes which were really good. I don't have any ideas to improve this recipe.

Love(3x) this soup! Didn't change anything. Just doubled the recipe 😂. My family always ask for this every time there's leftover ham. Thank you Chef John. Always enjoy your recipes. Please don't stop sharing.
I didn’t have to change a thing.
Wonderful recipe
only change was to use onion powder instead of an actual onion
